The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4205f51d8f1b130b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 87-88. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. statement: Let U be a four-dimensional coordinate ball B2, or a half-ball B+ 2 = B2 ∩ {x4 > 0}. Assume that the metric is smooth, C−1 g Id ≤ (gij) ≤ Cg Id, and that its coordinate C2 norm is at most Cg. Assume also uniformly bounded C3 norms for the charts and inverse charts. On a half-ball use boundary normal coordinates, so g44 = 1 and ga4 = 0 for a < 4. Let z be C3, up to the flat face when present, and constant on that face. Suppose, almost everywhere, that Az : Hessg z = G, Az = Id −(1 − e χ)ez ⊗ ez, ez = grad z | grad z| , 0 < χ0 ≤ e χ ≤ 1. (12.1) Here e χ and G are measurable. At grad z = 0, any measurable unit axis making the equation true is allowed. If | grad z| ≤ M1 and |G| ≤ N1, then there are α ∈ (0, 1), r0 > 0 and C < ∞ such that ∥ grad z∥Cα(U1) ≤ C(M1 + N1), Z Br(x)∩U | Hessg z|2 dVg ≤ C(M1 + N1)2 r2+2α (12.2) for x ∈ U1 and 0 < r ≤ r0, where U1 = B1 or B+ 1 . The constants depend only on χ0, the stated geometry bounds and the separation from the curved patch edges. The Cα norm may equivalently 87 be taken for the coordinate gradient components. In particular, no modulus of continuity of G or e χ, and no bound for a derivative of either, is assumed.
